key_results: Increasing d0 increases Δ, enlarges low-equivalence/unburned regions and destabilizes propagation; pre-evaporation restores stability by raising upstream gaseous fuel.
At φ_pre=0: d0=2,3,4 μm yield Δ=0.13,0.31,0.55 and velocities 1728,1696,1618 m/s; d0=5 μm gives Δ=0.84 and fails. Stability fit gives Δ≤0.72 without pre-evaporation.

mechanisms.summary: Author model: incomplete evaporation lowers local φ; transverse detonations may consume pockets until shock/flame decouple and quench.

evidence_candidates.claim: The paper defines Δ=L_E/L_D to compare droplet evaporation distance with detonation-front height.
For the simulated no-pre-evaporation family, increasing Δ produces larger unburned pockets and eventual shock–flame decoupling.
evidence_candidates.source_location: PDF p.12, Table 3 and quench discussion
